evidence.calendar_and_promotions: OBSERVED; not supplied to the planner in the main runs (sensitivity only)
evidence.demand_history: OBSERVED (track A) or DERIVED (track B, recovered)
evidence.opening_stock: SYNTHETIC: declared cover times DERIVED mean training demand
evidence.purchase_orders: SIMULATED by the replay, never observed
evidence.stockout_flags: OBSERVED; strata and recovery input only, never a policy outcome

knowledge_rule: END_OF_DAY_UTC: a day's sales and stock flags are knowable at 23:59:59 UTC of that day
note: Every value is a modelling assumption held identical across all evaluated policies; costs are indices per normalized unit, never currency; no purchase order, receipt, supplier or inventory record exists in the dataset.

supply.name: stable
supply.rationale: next-morning replenishment as the paper describes (06:00 restock); every order arrives in full

supply.name: uncertain
supply.rationale: two-day lead with one-day spread and short deliveries; a declared stress, not an observed supplier. NOTE: on daily periods a one-day lead spread exceeds the engine's half-period lateness slack, so the planner's supply-risk state activates (audit finding W1); this scenario therefore also exercises the protection regime, and the fill-only variant below separates the two effects

supply.name: uncertain_fill_only
supply.rationale: two-day lead, no lead spread, short deliveries: isolates fill uncertainty from the lateness state
